theme: 3 terms on loop control: ending a loop early, skipping one run and naming a loop to target it

terms.definition: A control-flow statement that ends a loop immediately and moves on to the code after it.
terms.example: Use breaks to stop the loop as soon as `score` is above 7.

terms.definition: A control-flow statement that skips the rest of the current run and starts the next one.
terms.example: Use continues to skip empty names and keep the loop going.

terms.definition: A control-flow statement that gives a loop a name, so `break` or `continue` can target that loop.
terms.example: Use labeled statements to leave the outer loop from inside the inner loop.

video.title: Break, Continue & Labeled Statement in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 22
video.description:
Learn to talk about controlling loops in Swift: Break, Continue & Labeled Statement, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Break - A control-flow statement that ends a loop immediately and moves on to the code after it.
Continue - A control-flow statement that skips the rest of the current run and starts the next one.
Labeled Statement - A control-flow statement that gives a loop a name, so `break` or `continue` can target that loop.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Break, Continue & Labeled Statement in English | Day 22
landscape.description:
Explain Break, Continue & Labeled Statement in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Break, Continue, 레이블 문 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Break - A control-flow statement that ends a loop immediately and moves on to the code after it.
한국어: Break 루프: 반복문을 즉시 끝내고 그 뒤 코드로 넘어가는 제어 흐름 문

Continue - A control-flow statement that skips the rest of the current run and starts the next one.
한국어: Continue 루프: 현재 실행의 나머지를 건너뛰고 다음 실행을 시작하는 제어 흐름 문

Labeled Statement - A control-flow statement that gives a loop a name, so `break` or `continue` can target that loop.
한국어: 레이블 문: 반복문에 이름을 붙여 break나 continue가 그 반복문을 가리키게 하는 제어 흐름 문

dialogue.title: Loop control in a chat

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, my loop checks every `score` in `rows`, but I want it to stop early.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use Break. When `score > 7`, Break leaves the loop right away.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So Break ends the whole loop, not only one run?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Some scores are `0`, and I want to skip those. Use Continue.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does Continue stop the loop too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. Continue skips the rest of this run and goes to the next `score`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But I have two loops. Break only leaves the inner one, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Add a Labeled Statement. Write `search:` before the outer loop.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, a Labeled Statement gives the loop a name, so `break search` leaves the outer loop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Continue can use that name too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. Break to stop, Continue to skip, Labeled Statement to pick the loop.
Use breaks to stop the loop early.
